We don’t do business with companies. We do business with people. Business is always human. 

Video from Globo (November 2025) in conversation with journalist Rodrigo Carvalho

"I'm an anxious person." "I'm an avoidant." "I'm just bad at this."
 
Listen to how you describe yourself for a day. Then count how many of those start with "I am."
 
As a psychotherapist, Amy Morin (@amymorinauthor) tells clients to try trading the being verb for a habit—“I have a tendency to,” “I do this sometimes.”
 
It sounds like a technicality, but it isn't. A tendency is something you can change next time. An identity is something you live up to.
 
What's one "I am" you'd swap?
 
This episode of A Bit of Optimism is brought to you by @sap 🎧 Check out the full episode wherever you get your podcasts!

We're told to stop worrying, but nobody ever tells us when to start.

Amy Morin (@amymorinauthor) is a psychotherapist and the author of 13 Things Mentally Strong People Don't Do. Her favorite exercise with clients starts from the opposite premise: worry gets a time and a place. Fifteen minutes in the calendar. And when it’s up, it’s up.

What I love about it is that you’re not denying or suppressing anything. You’re just allocating time for all that very healthy nonsense.

🎧 Listen to the full episode of A Bit of Optimism wherever you get your podcasts.

Optimism is not the denial of reality. It is the belief that even when things are dark, there is a way through.
⁣
In this special episode of Office Hours, Simon joins me to explore what optimism really requires. We discuss how optimism differs from hope, why relationships help us sustain our belief in a better future, how our expectations shape others, and why pessimism has become so powerful.
⁣
